script:
Good morning. Here's your briefing for Friday, September 18.

First up, AI & Tech.

First, OpenAI has launched its **Agents API** in public beta, giving developers direct access to the managed infrastructure behind advanced systems like Codex. This handles context, tools, and persistent execution for long-running AI agents, ideal for building sophisticated agents without complex orchestration.

OpenAI also rolled out **GPT-Live-1** in their API for five cents per minute. This new model brings full-duplex speech, allowing the AI to listen and speak simultaneously, naturally handle interruptions, and maintain conversational flow. Early tests show eighty percent fewer interruptions, making it a game-changer for highly interactive voice-based AI agents.

In open-source news, Alibaba Group has released **Open Code Review**, their internal AI-powered command-line interface tool. This battle-tested agent, having served tens of thousands of developers, identifies millions of code defects. It reads full files, searches codebases, and inspects changed files for context, offering deep, actionable code reviews for engineering teams.

A big competitive move comes from Cognition with **SWE-2**. This new model achieves fifty percent on the FrontierCode one-point-one Main One benchmark, while being sixty-four percent cheaper than its predecessor. It outperforms SWE-one-point-seven and Grok four-point-six in both score and cost. SWE-2 matches GPT-five-point-six Sol and Fable five/five-point-one at a fraction of their price and comes within a few points of GPT-six Astra at a quarter of the cost. So what for practitioners: This model offers significantly better code generation at a dramatically lower cost, making high-performance AI coding agents much more accessible for engineering teams.

Meta will soon announce a "Shared Agents" feature for its **Muse app**, allowing users to create and share customizable AI agents. This could benefit small businesses on Meta platforms for customer support.

Google has introduced a new **Google Cloud plugin for AI coding agents**. It provides installable bundles to equip your chosen AI agent with the skills and tools needed within Google Cloud environments.

Shifting to deeper technical insights, new research confirms that scaling web-video models and increasing pre-training compute leads to better robot task performance, even for complex industrial tasks. So what: This suggests readily available web video data can be a highly effective and scalable training method for developing more capable real-world robots.

Meta has also released **WearableQA**, a new benchmark for health reasoning, featuring thousands of questions built from real-world wearable data. So what: This provides a crucial new dataset and evaluation method for AI models performing health reasoning, essential for developing reliable medical AI applications.

Lastly, Salesforce research indicates that directly training smaller models on expert agent trajectories can negatively impact performance if the agent's harness is already optimized separately. So what: This highlights the importance of jointly optimizing both the AI agent and its surrounding orchestration layer to achieve optimal performance.

Briefly, OpenAI is reportedly considering slowing down cutting-edge AI development due to safety concerns, and they've paused Pro plan subscriptions due to high demand for their new Astra model.

Next, US Headlines.

House Speaker Mike Johnson has clarified that former President Trump's proposed five-thousand-dollar payments to Americans would require congressional approval. Trump maintains that the payouts would be easy to integrate into the federal budget, though some lawmakers are asking how they would be funded.

In political news, many vulnerable House Republicans are aligning themselves with former President Trump as the party seeks to defy historical trends in the upcoming midterm elections. This strategy aims to help the Republican Party retain or gain seats, traditionally a challenge for the party holding the White House.

Finally, former President Trump has dismissed warnings about the potential risks of artificial intelligence, expressing his view that the United States should not slow its development. He argues that the country must maintain its lead in AI, citing concerns about falling behind global competitors like China.

And finally, Immigration & Visas.

Good morning. Here's an update on US immigration and visa policy changes.

First, a significant proposed change for H one B visa holders: The Department of Homeland Security has put forth a rule that would eliminate the current 60-day grace period. This grace period typically allows H one B workers who lose their jobs to find new employment, change their visa status, or prepare to leave the country. If this proposal is finalized, H one B visa holders who lose their employment would no longer have this 60-day window. This directly impacts anyone currently on an H one B visa.

In other news, USCIS has made an administrative change regarding green cards. The agency has stopped sending the 'Welcome to America' packets to new green card recipients. This packet usually contained important information about living in the US as a permanent resident. While the physical packet is no longer being distributed, new green card holders will still receive their physical green card. This affects all new recipients of a green card, who will now need to find this information through other sources.

Finally, a trend impacting the H one B landscape: Reports indicate that some tech giants are silently rerouting jobs away from the United States. This move is attributed to the increasing costs associated with sponsoring H one B visas. While not a direct policy change, this trend could affect the availability of H one B sponsored roles within the US tech sector.

That's your briefing. Have a great day.
